equation_request.abstract: The software package Qcompiler Chen and Wang [2013] provides a general quantum compilation framework, which maps any given unitary operation into a quantum circuit consisting of a sequential set of elementary quantum gates. In this paper, we present an extended software OptQC, which finds permutation matrices $P$ and $Q$ for a given unitary matrix $U$ such that the number of gates in the quantum circuit of $U=Q^{T}P^{T}U^{\prime}PQ$ is significantly reduced, where $U^{\prime}$ is equivalent to $U$ up to a permutation and the quantum circuit implementation of each matrix component is considered separately. We extend further this software package to make use of high-performance computers with a multiprocessor architecture using MPI. We demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing the total number of quantum gates required for various unitary operators.

specification.problem: Given an explicit N x N unitary U with N=2^n (n=2 or 3), find basis permutation matrices P,Q so that U' = (PQ) U (PQ)^T is cheaper to compile, then synthesize U = Q^T P^T U' P Q as an ancilla-free, measurement-free circuit from standard gates. The runner reads the unitary or statevector and compares it with U up to global phase.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance (n=2 or 3, explicit classical U). Heuristic greedy-swap permutation search with a nonzero-entry count as the cost proxy. U' is compiled by a generic decomposition, and P and Q are compiled to X, CX and multi-controlled X gates. The circuit is applied to the all-zero input state, with the unitary or the statevector read out. Out of scope: the actual OptQC search, the Qcompiler internals, MPI parallelization, and any claim of gate-count savings.

equations.label: Permutation-conjugated factorization
equations.description: U is expressed through a permutation similarity transform of U'.
equations.justification: The abstract states this factorization directly.
assumptions: P and Q are real permutation matrices, so their inverses are their transposes

equations.label: Inverse relation for U'
equations.description: U' follows from eq_1 because PQ is orthogonal.
equations.justification: Left-multiplying eq_1 by PQ and right-multiplying by (PQ)^T gives this, since (PQ)^T(PQ)=I.
assumptions: The same permutation acts on both sides

equations.label: Search objective
equations.description: Heuristic minimization of a compiled-gate-count proxy.
equations.justification: The abstract reports reduced gate counts but gives no explicit objective, so this form is proposed.
assumptions: The cost proxy is the entry count plus the permutation circuit cost
The search is heuristic, not exhaustive

equations.label: Circuit operator and order
equations.latex: W = Q^{T}P^{T}\,C_{U^{\prime}}\,P\,Q,\quad \text{applied in time as } Q,\;P,\;C_{U^{\prime}},\;P^{T},\;Q^{T}
equations.description: The rightmost operator acts first in time.
equations.justification: Operator products act right to left, so Q is applied first.
assumptions: C_{U'} is an exact compilation of U'

equations.label: Initial state and output
equations.description: The circuit starts in |0...0>. The output state equals U|0...0> up to a global phase, and the full unitary matches U up to a global phase.
equations.justification: A statevector run needs a defined input, and all-zero is the default. The unitary comparison follows the task convention that global phase is unobservable.
assumptions: Little-endian: basis index k=sum_j b_j 2^j, with qubit j holding b_j

registers.name: q
registers.role: system qubits, little-endian index encoding, no ancillas

specification.initial_state: |0>^{\otimes n} (all qubits in |0>, basis index 0), with the circuit applying W so that the output is U|0...0> up to global phase

steps.description: Take U as an explicit matrix, fix the little-endian basis encoding, and start from |0...0>.
Heuristic greedy-swap search over basis permutations to minimize the cost proxy, yielding P, Q and U'.
Compile U' with a generic decomposition (Givens or cosine-sine into uniformly controlled Ry/Rz plus CX), skipping identity and zero blocks.
Compile P and Q as X, CX and multi-controlled X gates, preferring bitwise permutations (qubit swaps and X flips).
Assemble the circuit in the order Q, P, U', P^T, Q^T and compare its unitary or output state with U up to global phase.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical permutation search and matrix decomposition only. After assembly, compare the unitary or statevector with U up to global phase.
assumptions: Tiny instance (n=2 or 3) with explicit U
Entry count stands in for CNOT count
No ancillas, no measurements, no black box
U' is compiled by a generic decomposition standing in for Qcompiler
